q-cv-fit.label: Fill the blank with the best word
q-cv-fit.summary: A sentence with a blank; pick the word whose meaning matches the clue words around it.

rules.text: Check the part of speech first. If the blank needs a verb and one option is a noun, that option is out before meaning is even considered.
rules.ok: 'can ___ the inertia' needs a verb: dislodge, not 'persuasion'.
rules.bad: Choosing a noun for a verb slot.

rules.text: Find the clue words (an adjective or a second clause) that say what the blank must do, then choose the word whose meaning does that. Words such as entrenched, covert, dissent and austerity point to the sense.
rules.ok: 'Entrenched inertia' needs something to shift it: dislodge.
rules.bad: Choosing a word because it sounds learned.

q-cv-fit.cue: 'Select the correct option to fill in the blank' with a single word to place, usually an advanced verb.
q-cv-fit.standard: Read the sentence without the blank to see what job the word does; eliminate options of the wrong part of speech; pick the one whose meaning does that job.
q-cv-fit.fast: Underline the clue word (entrenched, covert, dissent) and turn it into a simple phrase ('shift something stuck', 'put down opposition'), then match.
q-cv-fit.eliminate: Remove the wrong part of speech first; then remove words whose meaning pulls the opposite way.
traps: One option is often a noun or adjective among verbs.
A word that sounds close in sense (disillusion, discourage) but has a different meaning.
A word that is the opposite of what is needed.

pyqs.text:
Select the correct option to fill in the blank.
Only a complete paradigm shift can ___ the deeply entrenched bureaucratic inertia.
pyqs.why: 'Entrenched' inertia is firmly fixed in place, so it takes something that forces it out: to dislodge it. A verb is needed after 'can'.

a.note: To discourage is to take away someone's confidence; inertia is a state, not a person to be put off.

c.note: To disillusion is to free someone from a false belief; it is about a person's beliefs, not a fixed habit.

d.note: 'Persuasion' is a noun; after 'can' the sentence needs a verb.

pyqs.trick: Entrenched = stuck in place; the verb must move it.

pyqs.text:
Select the correct option to fill in the blank.
The new rules, though seemingly driven by fiscal necessity, were actually a covert move to ___ dissent under "austerity."
pyqs.why: The rules are a hidden way to put down opposition, so the verb must mean to suppress: quell. 'Dissent' is the opposition being suppressed.

b.note: To impugn is to challenge someone's honesty; one does not impugn dissent itself, and it does not mean to suppress.

c.note: To swell would make dissent grow, the opposite of what a covert move to silence it would do.

d.note: To rebut is to answer an argument openly with evidence; a covert move is not a public reply.

practice.text:
Select the correct option to fill in the blank.
The council decided to ___ the festival to two days because of the budget.
practice.why: A budget problem makes the council shorten the festival: to curtail it.

a.note: To extend makes it longer, the opposite of what a shortage of money forces.

c.note: Celebrate does not take 'to two days' as a limit.

d.note: To mitigate is to make something harmful less severe; a festival is not a harm.

practice.text:
Select the correct option to fill in the blank.
Planting trees along the road can ___ the noise from traffic.
practice.why: The trees make the noise less severe: they mitigate it.

b.note: To reiterate is to repeat; one cannot repeat noise with trees.

c.note: To ostracise is to exclude a person from a group.

d.note: To cajole is to persuade by coaxing a person.

practice.text:
Select the correct option to fill in the blank.
He could not ___ his claim that the bridge was unsafe, because he had no report.
practice.why: A claim without a report cannot be supported: he cannot substantiate it.

a.note: To quell is to put down a disturbance, not support a claim.

c.note: To ostracise is to exclude a person.

d.note: To dislodge is to force something out of place.

practice.text:
Select the correct option to fill in the blank.
The villagers chose to ___ the family that had broken the custom, and nobody spoke to them.
practice.why: 'Nobody spoke to them' shows the family was excluded: ostracised.

a.note: To welcome is the opposite of what 'nobody spoke to them' shows.

c.note: To reiterate is to repeat something.

d.note: To substantiate is to support a claim with evidence.

practice.text:
Select the correct option to fill in the blank.
The teacher had to ___ the rule again because half the class had not understood it.
practice.why: She says the rule again for emphasis: she reiterates it.

b.note: To curtail is to cut short.

c.note: To quell is to suppress a disturbance.

d.note: To impugn is to challenge someone's honesty, which has nothing to do with a rule being repeated.

practice.text:
Select the correct option to fill in the blank.
She managed to ___ her reluctant brother into joining the trip with gentle flattery.
practice.why: Gentle flattery is the method of the verb to cajole.

a.note: To bully is to force by threat, but the sentence says 'gentle flattery'.

c.note: To dislodge is to force something from its place.

d.note: To rebut is to answer an argument.

practice.text:
Select the correct option to fill in the blank.
The opposition tried to ___ the minister's honesty by waving old letters in the House.
practice.why: Waving old letters to damage his honesty is an attempt to impugn it.

b.note: To quell is to suppress a disturbance.

c.note: To mitigate is to make something less severe.

d.note: To curtail is to cut short.

practice.text:
Select the correct option to fill in the blank.
The lawyer rose to ___ the charge with facts from the record.
practice.why: To answer a charge with facts is to rebut it.

b.note: To cajole is to coax; facts from a record are not coaxing.

c.note: To ostracise is to exclude a person.

d.note: To reiterate only repeats; the lawyer needs to answer the charge.

practice.text:
Select the correct option to fill in the blank.
A strong gust could ___ the loose tiles and send them down on the street.
practice.why: The gust forces the tiles out of their fixed place: it dislodges them.

b.note: To substantiate supports a claim with proof.

d.note: To cajole persuades a person by coaxing.

practice.text:
Select the correct option to fill in the blank.
Troops were sent in to ___ the riot before it spread to the next town.
practice.why: Troops sent to stop a riot are sent to quell it.

b.note: To cajole is to coax by flattery; troops do not coax a riot.

d.note: To substantiate is to support a claim with evidence.
